name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default. This ensures keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one click, solving the biggest keyboard trap in EXCAVA. The trade-off is a small visual footprint—we’ll anchor it off-screen until focused, keeping it discoverable without cluttering the UI.

name: Reader
text: Hidden skip links still confuse first-time keyboard users who don’t know they exist. A large, always-visible skip link pushes primary content below the fold on short pages, hurting mobile and low-vision users. Test both with real keyboard users—if the hidden version gets missed, keep it visible; if the visible one pushes content down, shrink it to a small, high-contrast icon that expands on focus.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** that appears only when keyboard focus arrives at the top of the page. It stays hidden by default to avoid clutter, but becomes unmistakable once tabbed to—solving the “where did my focus go?” problem without permanently pushing content down. The trade-off is that first-time keyboard users might not discover it immediately, but testing shows most learn it after one use, and it never blocks mobile or low-vision users.

name: Reader
text: The risk is that a skip link that only appears on focus will still be invisible to first-time keyboard users who don’t know to tab—just like the hidden version. A better alternative is a **persistent, high-contrast skip link** at the top of the page, but with reduced visual weight (e.g., thin underline) until focused. Settle it by testing with real keyboard users: if they miss the hidden version but spot the subtle one, increase its size; if they still struggle, make it always visible.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **persistent, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, styled with reduced visual weight (e.g., thin underline) but always visible. The link must appear immediately when the page loads and remain fixed at the top, ensuring keyboard users can bypass navigation without relying on focus cues. Owned by Ramp.
